paragraphs: Camis sells reservation and park management software to government-operated parks, marinas and harbors, work the company says it has done for more than 46 years. Visitors use it to book a camping trip, a day-use pass, a harbor stay or a ticketed event.

Bookings can come in ahead of time, at the gate, or through a call center. Payment runs through the same platform, whether the visitor is online or standing at a park office. A combined on-site and webstore system handles merchandise sales with real-time inventory tracking, and the company describes it as fully PCI and SOC compliant. Field staff get a separate enforcement app called Sidekick, built for the job assignments of wardens and rangers. On the back end, staff work from real-time data and customizable reports.

The company describes its origin as outdoor enthusiasts who saw a better way to connect people to parks. Its own timeline starts with a first park contract at Craigleith Provincial Park. The same timeline records that the business was acquired by Banyan Software. It also claims continued expansion across more than 30 national, provincial and state parks.

quote.text: Connecting People to a World of Memorable Experiences
